extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security Briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure only.
- **Delivery plane:** GitHub Actions workflow named **“Deploy to Azure”**.
- **Triggers:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch`, which means deployments can be initiated both by repository changes and manual invocation.
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted runner.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** No region, availability zone, multi-region, or redundant deployment topology is shown. The provided data does **not** indicate any HA or failover configuration.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- **Credential material:** Azure credentials are referenced as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **Risk:** The configuration indicates a secret-backed credential path, but the data does not show rotation, scoping, or separation per environment. Since OIDC is **not** used, the deployment depends on a stored secret rather than short-lived federation.
- **Plaintext-secret risk:** No plaintext secret is explicitly shown in the provided data. However, use of a GitHub Actions secret for cloud authentication increases exposure if workflow permissions, runner context, or secret handling are weak.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false` in aggregate signals.
- **Key management:** No key management, customer-managed keys, or encryption policy is shown.
- **Risk:** The configuration set does not demonstrate encryption-at-rest coverage for stored data or artifacts. This is a material control gap.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity`
- **Principal:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`
- **Scope:** `subscription`
- **Trust principal:** `github-actions`
- **OIDC:** Not used.
- **Risk:** Subscription-scoped access is broad and may exceed least-privilege for a deployment pipeline. The trust model relies on a stored secret rather than federated identity, which is less resistant to secret leakage. The data does not show role scoping, resource-group restriction, or conditional access controls.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner model:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted runner.
- **OIDC posture:** Disabled (`uses_oidc: false`).
- **Workflow trigger surface:** `push` + `workflow_dispatch` increases the execution surface; manual dispatch can be useful but should be tightly governed.
- **Risk:** Hosted runners introduce a shared execution environment. Without OIDC, the pipeline is more dependent on static credentials in GitHub Actions secrets.

### 6) Container security
- **No container node is present** in the provided data.
- Therefore, **root container usage, health checks, and resource limits cannot be assessed** from the available configuration.

### 7) Key risks and recommendations
1. **Replace static Azure credentials with OIDC federation.**  
   This removes long-lived secret dependence and improves credential hygiene for GitHub Actions.

2. **Reduce IAM scope from subscription-level to the minimum required resource scope.**  
   Prefer resource-group or resource-level permissions with explicit role assignment.

3. **Establish encryption-at-rest and document key management.**  
   Enable encryption coverage and define whether Microsoft-managed keys or customer-managed keys are required, including rotation and access control.

## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points**
  - `FastAPI` calls four API endpoints: **Login**, **Me**, **Logout**, and **Chat Endpoint**.
  - **Bearer Auth** protects **Chat Endpoint**, **Login**, **Logout**, **Me**, and **Generic**.

- **Orchestration / agent flow**
  - `OpenAI Agents` framework calls all five agents: **Triage**, **Flight Status**, **FAQ**, **Cancellation**, and **Seat Booking**.
  - `Triage Agent` delegates to **Flight Status Agent** and **FAQ Agent**.

- **Model use**
  - All five agents use **gpt-4.1-mini**.
  - Both guardrails also use **gpt-4.1-mini**:
    - **Relevance Guardrail**
    - **Jailbreak Guardrail**

- **Tool access**
  - `OpenAI Agents` framework can call these tools directly: **Baggage Tool**, **Cancel Flight**, **Display Seat Map**, **Faq Lookup Tool**, **Flight Status Tool**, **Lookup Reservation**, and **Update Seat**.
  - `Triage`, `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, and `Seat Booking` agents can call overlapping sets of tools.
  - Notably, **Seat Booking Agent** has tool access but no delegation path shown from `Triage`.

- **Data stores**
  - `Sqlite` appears with **no connections** shown, so no datastore access is represented in the graph.

- **Security observations**
  - Guardrail coverage is shown only for **Relevance** and **Jailbreak** checks; no other guardrails are shown for tools or data access.
  - Several tools are reachable directly by the `OpenAI Agents` framework, which is a notable broad-access pattern.
  - No sensitive datastore connections are shown, and `Sqlite` is currently disconnected.
